steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Place bread crumbs into a small bowl and mix well with melted butter; set aside.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add macaroni and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes; drain, then place into the prepared casserole dish.
While pasta is cooking, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in minced onion and cook until onion softens and turns translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour, salt, pepper, and dry mustard until incorporated, then pour in milk and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until milk has thickened, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in Cheddar cheese until melted. Pour cheese sauce over macaroni, then sprinkle evenly with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is golden and bubbly, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Easy baked macaroni and cheese made from scratch with onion and cheddar cheese. There's a bit of dry mustard in the mac and cheese for zip.
raw_recipe.name: Macaroni and Cheese

review.reviewBody: This is a good base recipe but needs just a bit of tweeking. 1. Because I have a picky toddler I avoided the onions. 2. When making the sauce, add 1 cup of milk to your sauce pan and reserve 1/2 a cup cold milk to mix your dry ingredients in. Mix the dry ingredients into the 1/2 cup cold milk and mix thoroughly--you will prevent lumps this way. Add the remaining 1/2 cup and stir. I found it didn't thicken very well until I added the cheese. I kept the cheese on the heat until the sauce thickened. 3. I recommend adding a second cheese. I added romano but parmasean, monteray Jack or any other sharp cheese would really enhance the flavour. 4. I crushed up 2 crackers and put them on top, I sprayed a bit of olive oil onto them to allow for browning. I also grated a bit of cheedar cheese onto the bread crumbs maybe 2-3 tbsp.

Added finely cut strips of proscuitto ham to middle of casserole and sprinkled parmesan on top instead of breadcrumbs. I also preferred to make a roux for the cheese sauce and used shell macaroni and a blend of cheddar, asiago and gouda, without onions.
I made this without breadcrumbs and it was a hit with the family.

This was a great mac and cheese recipe in itself. I loved that it called for onions and mustard powder and I found the recipe to be quite versatile - I just used a bunch of leftover bits of cheese (cheddar, Gruyere, pepper jack, mozzarella). Unfortunately, I think the bread crumbs really took over and ruined an otherwise delicious flavor. Next time, I'll either skip them altogether or substitute crushed Ritz crackers or crushed corn flakes spritzed with melted butter. Without the breadcrumbs, I think this recipe would have been a four-star. Thanks for sharing!
Update: this time I used crushed Ritz crackers (no butter) and it was MUCH better. It did come out a little dry though. Next time, I'll try making 50% more cheese sauce -- it seems to really soak into the pasta as it bakes.

This is pretty good. It seems like a lot of cheese sauce for a small amount of pasta, so I doubled the pasta. I do have a trick for sauces that require long stirring - warm the milk to lukewarm in the microwave before adding. Cuts down a little bit on the time to reach simmer, hence, less time spent stirring.

I use this exact recipe except for one little secret of mine...I add 1 tablespoon of Worcerstershire Sauce in addition to the ground mustard. That makes a big difference! Also I omit the breadcrumbs but instead sprinkle some reserved shredded cheese to the top before baking..the cheese gets a nice crusty brown. I use half sharp cheddar and half Mexican or Colby Jack cheese. I have made this with and without the onion and it's delicious both ways. What I love about this recipe is you can make it up ahead of time and keep in frig until ready to bake. Great recipe, lots of raves on this. Everywhere I go everyone asks for this. I agree with another reviewer...add half the milk to the flour and butter and whisk until not lumpy. Then add the remaining milk. Much easier and no lumps!

This dish is so yummy! I change it a little and use 1 T. fresh mustard and instead of bread crumbs on top, i use about half a roll of ritz crackers and crush them up and add them to a half a stick of butter and then put on top! We make it all the time and all our kids LOVE it! Its the best!

Made this for Thanksgiving and everyone loved it...the only changes i made: I added about 1/4 cup of sour cream to the cheese sauce While baking, i poured in extra milk and stirred to keep it creamy Also added 2 teaspoons of dry mustard. I made this recipe 3 times and believe me the changes made a difference.

I have made this exactly as directed & get many compliments. I do like my own tweeks too; I use a high quality very sharp chedder cheese, tsp of regular spicy brown mustard or grey poupon (rather than the dried) & add a bit of regular Mrs. Dash to taste (in addition to salt & pepper). I wisk the milk sauce rather than stir it to make it real smooth. I lOVE the breadcrumbs on top, but my family doesn't so I put the crumbs over 1/2 of it for a delicious thick breadcrumb crust for me :-)

I try all my recipes with ricemilk & do not recommend using ricemilk for this one. However, the ricemilk version was still SO MUCH better than storebought boxed stuff. Also, this does seem to need a bit salt. I tried without it, but found I needed a little to taste as good (& I never cook with salt).

This was pretty good. It's a great starter recipe but definitely needs some additional spices. I love the sauce. If you add the milk slowly you shouldn't get "grains." My texture was just fine! I used half mozzarella and half cheddar. Also, definitely mix your noodles into the sauce before putting them in the greased pan. The noodles on the bottom had nothing on them :( I'll be doing that next time for sure. It was a decent recipe though! Thanks for posting!

This was really good and very easy. Instead of just using Cheddar Cheese I did half cheddar and half Jack. I also doubled the recipe to fit it in a 13x9 inch pan. My husband loves spice so he added some Tapatio to the top for some extra flavor. I usually add Chipotle Tabasco. :)
i’ve been making this recipe for more than 10 years. It is perfect, delicious and easy. Good with or without the onions.
YUM! This is the same recipe that my Mom and Grandma always used. I believe it came from a macaroni box originally. I make this with 12 ounces of pasta instead of 8.
the dry mustard just adds a nice zip!
I made this with vegan substitutes and it was amazing!! I baked it with croutons on top and added crispy onions when served.
I made it exactly like the recipe said. Next time I would put the cooked pasta back in the pot and mix the cheese sauce in and then put them both into the casserole.

Very tasty! My husband loved it.
Next time will try using wipped butter to cut down on the fat content.
If you want this to turn out REALLY authentic and delicious beyond belief, add one or two beaten eggs to the mixture before baking. :)
It was just like my mother used to make. Only thing I would cut back on the bread crumbs. But my family loved it!
